forbidden_behavior: read a heap block after free() has released it (the --uaf path)
valid_domain: argv[1] is a C string of length 0..4096; the copy keeps at most 49 bytes
valid_behavior: print argv[1] followed by one LF on stdout and exit 0, on both paths
invalid_behavior: on --uaf the released block must still print its original text, never allocator sentinel bytes
authorized_edits: Move the read of the buffer before free() in badSink, or drop the free()-then-read ordering; no other behaviour may change.
Allow up to 128 bytes of added x86-64 code in a gate-3-verified unused region of a loadable R-X segment; zero bytes alone are not evidence.
Allow no new segment, dynamic import, GOT/PLT/relocation edit or permission broadening beyond the existing contract rules.
environment_assumptions: glibc tcache serves the same-size follow-up malloc from the just-freed block; this makes the hazard observable without a sanitizer and is not a language guarantee
CET: ENDBR64 is compile-time only; runtime IBT/shadow-stack enforcement is not verified
